items.description: The Trump administration moved on multiple fronts Thursday to contain surging energy prices driven by the war with Iran, granting India a 30-day waiver to purchase sanctioned Russian crude and signaling it may take the unprecedented step of intervening in oil futures markets.

items.title: EU split deepens over rolling back climate rules to cut energy costs

featured_image.name: European Union proposes world's strictest emissions rules ...

items.description: European governments are retreating from key climate commitments as the economic fallout from the loss of cheap Russian energy collides with mounting industrial pressure to lower power prices. With EU leaders set to tackle electricity costs at a summit on March 19, a deepening rift has emerged between member states over how far to roll back the bloc's climate architecture.

items.title: US reports 90 percent drop in Iranian ballistic missile attacks

featured_image.name: Number of Iranian ballistic missiles fired plunges since start of Operation  Epic Fury

items.description: Iranian ballistic missile attacks have plummeted by 90 percent since the start of Operation Epic Fury, U.S. Central Command chief Adm. Brad Cooper announced Thursday during a press briefing at CENTCOM headquarters in Tampa, Florida. Drone attacks have fallen by 83 percent over the same period, Cooper said, as U.S. and Israeli forces continue to degrade Tehran's offensive military capabilities in what has become the largest American buildup in the Middle East in a generation.[1][2]

items.title: Trump urges Iranian diplomats worldwide to seek asylum

featured_image.name: Donald Trump bets big on the Iran war

items.description:
President Donald Trump called on Iranian diplomats around the world to request asylum and help shape "a new and better Iran" during a White House event on Thursday, as the US and Israel pressed ahead with a military campaign now in its sixth day.

"We also urge Iranian diplomats around the world to request asylum and to help us shape a new and better Iran with great potential," Trump said at a ceremony honoring Inter Miami's 2025 MLS Cup championship, before pivoting to an extended briefing on the conflict.[1][2]

items.title: Iran warns EU will 'pay the price' for silence on war

featured_image.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran- Iran Foreign  Ministry Spokesman rejects EU officials claims as baseless

items.description: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei warned European Union countries on Thursday that they will "pay the price, sooner or later" if they remain silent on the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran, which Tehran considers a violation of international law. The remarks, made during an interview with Spanish public broadcaster TVE, came as the conflict entered its sixth day with no sign of de-escalation.[1][2][3]

items.title: UAE weighs freezing billions in Iranian assets

featured_image.name: Exclusive | U.A.E. Explores Freezing Iranian Assets to ...

items.description:
The United Arab Emirates is considering freezing billions of dollars in Iranian assets held within the Gulf state, a move that could sever a key economic lifeline for Tehran as the conflict between the U.S., Israel, and Iran enters its second week, according to The Wall Street Journal.[1]

The potential asset freeze comes as Iran continues to pummel the UAE with missiles and drones in retaliation for the U.S.-Israeli strikes that killed Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei late last month. As of March 4, the UAE defense ministry reported intercepting 175 of 189 ballistic missiles and 876 of 941 drones launched against the country since February 28, with the attacks killing three foreign nationals and injuring 78 others.[2][3]

items.title: Australians on US sub sat out operation to sink Iranian ship, PM says
items.description: The prime minister has confirmed three Royal Australian Navy personnel were on board a US submarine that sank an Iranian warship earlier this week.

items.title: Trump says Iran seeking deal as US strikes continue

featured_image.name: Trump says Iran is 'running out of launchers' as regime is 'being ...

items.description:
President Donald Trump declared on Thursday that Iran is calling the United States to negotiate a deal, even as US and Israeli military operations against the country showed no signs of slowing. Speaking at a White House event celebrating Inter Miami CF's MLS Cup championship, Trump pivoted to the war in Iran, claiming the Iranian regime was seeking an end to hostilities but that Washington was in no rush to stop fighting.

"They're calling, they're saying, 'How do we make a deal?' I said, 'You're being a little bit late,'" Trump said, according to remarks reported by the Jerusalem Post and the Straits Times. "And we want to fight now more than they do."[1][2]

items.title: Ukraine, Russia swap 200 POWs each as peace talks stall over Iran war

featured_image.name: Russia and Ukraine start biggest prisoner swap of the war

items.description: U.S.-brokered peace talks between Ukraine and Russia, originally planned for this week, have been postponed indefinitely as the escalating conflict in the Middle East pulls international focus away from ending the four-year war in Eastern Europe. Despite the diplomatic setback, the two sides carried out a major prisoner exchange on Thursday, returning hundreds of soldiers to their families.

items.title: Russia and Ukraine begin swapping 500 POWs each over two days

featured_image.name: Russia, Ukraine to exchange 500 prisoners of war on March 5 ...

items.description:
Russia and Ukraine exchanged 200 prisoners of war on each side on Thursday and plan to swap another 300 each on Friday, the Russian Foreign Ministry said, in what amounts to the largest single exchange between the two countries in months.[1]

Vladimir Medinsky, Russia's lead negotiator and an aide to President Vladimir Putin, announced the exchange on his Telegram channel, saying it was "part of the agreements reached in Geneva," referring to the latest round of trilateral peace talks between Russia, Ukraine, and the United States. Russia's Defense Ministry said the United Arab Emirates and the U.S. helped mediate Thursday's swap of the first 200 on each side.[2][3]

items.title: Over 330,000 displaced across Middle East, UNHCR says

featured_image.name: Israeli bombardment of Lebanon sends 100,000 fleeing to war-torn Syria: UN

items.description:
More than 330,000 people have been forcibly displaced across the Middle East and beyond as intensifying hostilities between the United States, Israel, and Iran send shockwaves through a region already hosting millions of refugees, the UN refugee agency said Thursday.[1][2]

UNHCR reported that an estimated 100,000 people fled Tehran in the first 48 hours after US-Israeli strikes began on February 28, with road police recording between 1,000 and 2,000 vehicles departing the capital daily, heading primarily toward northern provinces. Despite the internal exodus, the agency noted "no major increase in cross-border movements from Iran linked to recent events".[3][2][1]
